readings.title: Balak Sends for Balaam
readings.subtitle: The King of Mo’aḇ’s Fear
readings.text: [Numbers 22:1] And the children of Yisra’el set out and camped in the desert plains of Mo’aḇ beyond the Yardĕn of Yeriḥo. [2] And Balaq son of Tsippor saw all that Yisra’el had done to the Amorites. [3] And Mo’aḇ was exceedingly afraid of the people because they were many, and Mo’aḇ was in dread because of the children of Yisra’el. [4] And Mo’aḇ said to the elders of Miḏyan, “Now this company is licking up all that is around us, as an ox licks up the grass of the field.” And Balaq son of Tsippor was sovereign of the Mo’aḇites at that time. [5] And he sent messengers to Bil’am son of Be’or at Pethor, which is near the River in the land of the sons of his people, to call him, saying, “See, a people has come out from Mitsrayim. See, they have covered the face of the earth, and are settling next to me! [6] “And now, please come at once, curse this people for me, for they are too strong for me. It might be that I strike them and drive them out of the land, for I know that he whom you bless is blessed, and he whom you curse is cursed.” [7] And the elders of Mo’aḇ and the elders of Miḏyan left with the fees for divination in their hand, and they came to Bil’am and spoke to him the words of Balaq. [8] And he said to them, “Stay here tonight, and I shall bring back word to you, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> speaks to me.” So the heads of Mo’aḇ stayed with Bil’am. [9] And <dn>Elohim</dn> came to Bil’am and said, <dq>“Who are these men with you?”</dq> [10] And Bil’am said to <dn>Elohim</dn>, “Balaq son of Tsippor, sovereign of Mo’aḇ, has sent to me, saying, [11] ‘See, a people has come out of Mitsrayim, and it covers the face of the earth. Come now, curse them for me, it might be that I am able to fight against them and drive them out.’ ” [12] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said to Bil’am, <dq>“Do not go with them, you do not curse the people, for they are blessed.”</dq> [13] And Bil’am rose in the morning and said to the heads of Balaq, “Go back to your land, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has refused to allow me to go with you.” [14] And the heads of Mo’aḇ rose up and went to Balaq, and said, “Bil’am refuses to come with us.” [15] And Balaq again sent heads, more numerous and more esteemed than they. [16] And they came to Bil’am and said to him, “This is what Balaq son of Tsippor said, ‘Please let nothing hinder you from coming to me, [17] ‘for I esteem you very highly, and whatever you say to me I do. Therefore please come, curse this people for me.’ ” [18] And Bil’am answered and said to the servants of Balaq, “Though Balaq were to give me his house filled with silver and gold, I am unable to go beyond the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> my <dn>Elohim</dn>, to do little or large. [19] “And now, please, you also stay here tonight, and let me know what more <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> says to me.” [20] And <dn>Elohim</dn> came to Bil’am at night and said to him, <dq>“If the men come to call you, rise and go with them, but only the word which <dn>I</dn> speak to you, that you do.”</dq>

readings.title: Balaam and the Messenger
readings.subtitle: The Speaking Donkey
readings.text: [Numbers 22:21] And Bil’am rose in the morning and saddled his donkey, and went with the heads of Mo’aḇ. [22] And the displeasure of <dn>Elohim</dn> burned because he was going, and the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> stationed <dn>Himself</dn> in the way as an adversary against him. And he was riding on his donkey, and his two servants were with him. [23] And the donkey saw the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> standing in the way with <dn>His</dn> drawn sword in <dn>His</dn> hand, and the donkey turned aside out of the way and went into the field. So Bil’am struck the donkey to turn it back onto the way. [24] Then the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> stood in a narrow path between the vineyards, with a wall on this side and a wall on that side. [25] And when the donkey saw the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, it pushed itself against the wall and crushed Bil’am’s foot against the wall. So he struck it again. [26] And the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> went further, and stood in a narrow place where there was no way to turn either to the right or to the left. [27] And when the donkey saw the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, it lay down under Bil’am. And Bil’am’s displeasure burned, and he struck the donkey with his staff. [28] Then <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> opened the mouth of the donkey, and it said to Bil’am, “What have I done to you, that you have struck me these three times?” [29] And Bil’am said to the donkey, “Because you have mocked me. I wish there were a sword in my hand, for I would have killed you by now!” [30] And the donkey said to Bil’am, “Am I not your donkey on which you have ridden, ever since I became yours, to this day? Was I ever known to do so to you?” And he said, “No.” [31] Then <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> opened Bil’am’s eyes, and he saw the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> standing in the way with <dn>His</dn> drawn sword in <dn>His</dn> hand. And he bowed his head and fell on his face. [32] And the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him, <dq>“Why have you struck your donkey these three times? See, <dn>I</dn> have come out to stand against you, because your way is reckless before <dn>Me</dn>.</dq> [33] <dq>“And the donkey saw <dn>Me</dn> and turned aside from <dn>Me</dn> these three times. If it had not turned aside from <dn>Me</dn>, <dn>I</dn> would have killed you by now, and let it live.”</dq> [34] And Bil’am said to the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “I have sinned, for I did not know <dn>You</dn> stood in the way against me. And now, if it is evil in <dn>Your</dn> eyes, I shall go back.” [35] And the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Bil’am, <dq>“Go with the men, but only the word <dn>I</dn> speak to you, that you speak.”</dq> So Bil’am went with the heads of Balaq. [36] And when Balaq heard that Bil’am was coming, he went out to meet him at the city of Mo’aḇ, which is on the border of the Arnon, at the utmost boundary. [37] And Balaq said to Bil’am, “Did I not urgently send to you, to call you? Why did you not come to me? Am I not able to esteem you?” [38] And Bil’am said to Balaq, “See, I have come to you! Am I at all able to say somewhat? The word that <dn>Elohim</dn> puts in my mouth, that I speak.” [39] And Bil’am went with Balaq, and they came to Qiryath Ḥutsoth. [40] And Balaq slaughtered cattle and sheep, and he sent some to Bil’am and to the heads who were with him. [41] And it came to be, in the morning, that Balaq took Bil’am and brought him up to the high places of Ba’al, and from there he saw the extremity of the people.

readings.title: Balaam’s First Oracle
readings.subtitle: A People Set Apart
readings.text: [Numbers 23:1] And Bil’am said to Balaq, “Build seven altars for me here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me here.” [2] And Balaq did as Bil’am had said, and Balaq and Bil’am offered a bull and a ram on each altar. [3] And Bil’am said to Balaq, “Stand by your burnt offering, and let me go. It might be that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> comes to meet me, and whatever <dn>He</dn> shows me I shall certainly tell you.” And he went to a bare height. [4] And <dn>Elohim</dn> met Bil’am, and he said to <dn>Him</dn>, “I have prepared the seven altars, and I have offered a bull and a ram on each altar.” [5] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> put a word in Bil’am’s mouth, and said, <dq>“Return to Balaq, and this is what you say.”</dq> [6] So he returned to him, and see, he was standing by his burnt offering, he and all the heads of Mo’aḇ. [7] And he took up his oracle and said, “From Aram Balaq has brought me, the sovereign of Mo’aḇ, from the mountains of the East: ‘Come, curse Ya’aqoḇ for me, and come, rage against Yisra’el!’ [8] “How do I curse whom <dn>El</dn> has not cursed? And how do I rage against whom <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has not raged? [9] “For from the top of the rocks I see him, and from the hills I observe him. See, a people dwelling alone, not reckoning itself among the nations. [10] “Who shall count the dust of Ya’aqoḇ, and the number of one-fourth of Yisra’el? Let me die the death of the upright, and let my end be like his!” [11] And Balaq said to Bil’am, “What have you done to me? I took you to curse my enemies, and see, you have blessed them instead!” [12] And he answered and said, “Should I not take heed to speak what <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> puts in my mouth?”

readings.title: Balaam’s Second Oracle
readings.subtitle: Elohim is Not a Man
readings.text: [Numbers 23:13] And Balaq said to him, “Please come with me to another place from which you see them – you see only the extremity of them, and do not see them all – and curse them for me from there.” [14] So he took him to the field of Tsophim, to the top of Pisgah, and built seven altars, and offered a bull and a ram on each altar. [15] And he said to Balaq, “Stand here by your burnt offering while I meet over there.” [16] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> met Bil’am, and put a word in his mouth, and said, <dq>“Return to Balaq, and this is what you say.”</dq> [17] And he came to him, and see, he was standing by his burnt offering, and the heads of Mo’aḇ with him. And Balaq said to him, “What has <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoken?” [18] And he took up his oracle and said, “Rise up, Balaq, and hear! Listen to me, son of Tsippor! [19] “<dn>El</dn> is not a man, to lie, nor a son of man, to repent. Has <dn>He</dn> said, and does <dn>He</dn> not do it? Or has <dn>He</dn> spoken, and does <dn>He</dn> not establish it? [20] “See, I have received to bless, and <dn>He</dn> has blessed, and I do not reverse it. [21] “<dn>He</dn> has not looked upon wickedness in Ya’aqoḇ, nor has <dn>He</dn> seen trouble in Yisra’el. <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> his <dn>Elohim</dn> is with him, and the shout of a Sovereign is in him. [22] “<dn>El</dn> brought them out of Mitsrayim, <dn>He</dn> has as it were the horns of a wild ox for them. [23] “For there is no sorcery against Ya’aqoḇ, nor is there any divination against Yisra’el. Now it is said to Ya’aqoḇ and to Yisra’el, ‘What has <dn>El</dn> done!’ [24] “See, a people rises like a lioness, and lifts itself up like a lion; it does not lie down until it eats the prey, and drinks the blood of the slain.” [25] And Balaq said to Bil’am, “Neither curse them at all, nor bless them at all!” [26] But Bil’am answered and said to Balaq, “Did I not speak to you, saying, ‘All that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> speaks, that I do’?”

readings.title: Balaam’s Third Oracle
readings.subtitle: The Beauty of the Tents
readings.text: [Numbers 23:27] And Balaq said to Bil’am, “Please come, let me take you to another place. It might be right in the eyes of <dn>Elohim</dn> that you curse them for me from there.” [28] And Balaq took Bil’am to the top of Pe’or, that looks down on the wasteland. [29] And Bil’am said to Balaq, “Build seven altars for me here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me here.” [30] And Balaq did as Bil’am had said, and offered a bull and a ram on each altar. [Numbers 24:1] And when Bil’am saw that it pleased <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to bless Yisra’el, he did not go as at other times, to seek for sorcery, but he set his face toward the wilderness. [2] And Bil’am lifted up his eyes and saw Yisra’el encamped according to their tribes. And the Spirit of <dn>Elohim</dn> came upon him. [3] And he took up his oracle and said, “The oracle of Bil’am son of Be’or, and the oracle of the man whose eyes are opened, [4] “the oracle of him who hears the words of <dn>El</dn>, who sees the vision of <dn>Shaddai</dn>, who falls down, with eyes opened: [5] “How lovely are your tents, O Ya’aqoḇ, your dwellings, O Yisra’el! [6] “Like wadis that stretch out, like gardens by a river, like aloes planted by <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, like cedars beside the waters. [7] “He makes water flow from his buckets, and his seed is in many waters. His sovereign is higher than Agag̱, and his reign is exalted. [8] “<dn>El</dn> brought him out of Mitsrayim, he has as it were the horns of a wild ox for him. He devours nations, his enemies, and he breaks their bones and strikes with his arrows. [9] “He bowed down, he lay down like a lion. And like a lioness, who rouses him? He who blesses you is blessed, and he who curses you is cursed.” [10] Then Balaq’s displeasure burned against Bil’am, and he struck his hands together. And Balaq said to Bil’am, “I called you to curse my enemies, and see, you have kept on blessing them these three times! [11] “And now, flee to your place. I said I would greatly esteem you, but see, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has kept you back from esteem.” [12] And Bil’am said to Balaq, “Did I not also speak to your messengers whom you sent to me, saying, [13] ‘If Balaq were to give me his house filled with silver and gold, I am unable to go beyond the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to do either good or evil of my own heart. What <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> speaks, that I speak’? [14] “And now, see, I am going to my people. Come, let me advise you what this people is going to do to your people in the latter days.”

readings.title: Balaam’s Final Oracle
readings.subtitle: The Star of Ya’aqoḇ
readings.text: [Numbers 24:15] And he took up his oracle and said, “The oracle of Bil’am son of Be’or, and the oracle of the man whose eyes are opened, [16] “the oracle of him who hears the words of <dn>El</dn>, and knows the knowledge of <dn>the Most High</dn>, who sees the vision of <dn>Shaddai</dn>, who falls down, with eyes opened: [17] “I see <dn>Him</dn>, but not now; I observe <dn>Him</dn>, but not near. A Star shall come out of Ya’aqoḇ, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Yisra’el, and shall smite the corners of Mo’aḇ, and shall destroy all the sons of Sheth. [18] “And Eḏom shall be a possession, and Se’ir shall be a possession – enemies – and Yisra’el shall do mightily. [19] “And from Ya’aqoḇ one shall rule and shall destroy the remnant from the city.” [20] And he saw Amaleq, and he took up his oracle and said, “Amaleq was first of the nations, but his latter end is to perish.” [21] And he saw the Qĕynite, and he took up his oracle and said, “Your dwelling place is strong, and your nest is set in the rock; [22] “but the Qĕynite is to be consumed. How long before Ashshur takes you away captive?” [23] And he took up his oracle and said, “Alas, who shall live when <dn>El</dn> does this? [24] “And ships shall come from the coast of Kittim, and they shall afflict Ashshur and afflict Ěḇer, and he too shall perish.” [25] Then Bil’am rose up and left and returned to his place. And Balaq also went his way.
